cards.text: Joshua is leading Israel now (Joshua 1:1-2). The two spies he sent to Jericho came back saying the LORD has delivered the whole land into their hands, and early the next morning Joshua leaves Shittim with ALL the Israelites (Joshua 2:1, 23-24). Friend, I've watched four people take forty minutes to find their keys, so a whole camp moving out at sunrise has me SHOOK.

cards.question: Joshua and all the Israelites leave Shittim and go as far as the ___ River, where they camp before crossing over.

cards.text: Three days they wait by that river, which for me would mean reorganizing the sprinkle shelf FOUR times. Then the officers go through the camp with orders: watch for the ark of the covenant of the LORD, carried by the Levitical priests.

cards.question: When the people see the priests carrying the ark of the covenant, what are they told to do?

answers.text: Set out from their spots and follow it
Bow down and stay in their tents
Gather around it and wait for Joshua

cards.question: The officers also tell the people to stay about two thousand cubits back from the ark. Why such a big gap?

answers.text: So they can see the way to go
So the dust stays off the ark
So the priests can walk faster

cards.text: Two thousand cubits of personal space, and I spent YEARS in a junk drawer pressed up against a rubber band! Then Joshua tells the people to consecrate themselves, and I bet every ear in that camp perks RIGHT up.

cards.question: Joshua tells the people to consecrate themselves. What reason does he give?

answers.text: Tomorrow the LORD will do wonders among them
Tomorrow the priests will offer sacrifices
Tomorrow the kings of Canaan will attack

cards.text: Joshua tells the priests to take the ark and go on ahead of the people, and out front they go, no arguing, no five more minutes. Then the LORD tells Joshua that today He'll begin to exalt him in the sight of all Israel.

cards.question: The LORD says He'll exalt Joshua so all Israel may know He is with Joshua just as He was with ___.
The LORD tells Joshua that the priests carrying the ark should stay on the bank and keep their feet out of the Jordan.

cards.text: Joshua calls everybody in to hear the words of the LORD their God: here's how you'll know the living God is among you and will surely drive out the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites and Jebusites. SEVEN nations in one breath, friend, and I run out of air reading the back of a cookie box.

cards.question: Joshua says to choose twelve men, and all twelve come from the tribe of Levi.
Joshua says the ark will go ahead of them into the Jordan. When the priests' feet touch the water, what will the flowing water do?

answers.text: Stop and stand up in a heap
Rise up and flood the camp
Drop down to a shallow stream

cards.text: So the people break camp, and the priests carry the ark out in front. Now hold on, friend, because you need to know something about the Jordan at harvest time.

cards.question: During the harvest season, the Jordan runs low and easy to cross.

cards.text: Overflowing its banks. Of COURSE it is, right when they need to cross, like the one morning you're running early and the whole highway turns into a parking lot.

The SECOND the priests' feet touch the water's edge, the flowing water stands still, backing up as far as Adam, a city near Zarethan, while the water headed to the Salt Sea is completely cut off. Friend, I've hit the OFF switch on a mixer and it STILL spun longer than that.

cards.question: With the river cut off, the people cross over opposite Jericho.
In the middle of the Jordan, the priests with the ark stand firm on ___ ground until the entire ___ has crossed.

cards.text: Keep that apron on and stay close, friend, because Joshua and Israel aren't finished here yet.

findings.problem: Card 14 cites only Joshua 3:14, but its second sentence brings in the Jordan at harvest time, which comes from Joshua 3:15. The citation is narrower than what the card tells.

rule.text: Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The setup line "Now hold on, friend, because you need to know something about the Jordan at harvest time" signals a complication. That tips the baker toward False on card 15 and rules out the True answer before they reason it out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 16 restates the answer card 15 just revealed (the Jordan overflowing its banks at harvest) and adds a joke. It doesn't move the passage forward. The highway joke should ride on a card that carries the next moment, such as card 17, or this card should be cut.

rule.text: Every story card moves the baker forward through the passage. No recap cards.

findings.problem: The passage flow breaks here. Card 11 ends on Joshua's "here's how you'll know" without saying how. Card 12 then jumps to the twelve men (3:12). Only after that does card 13 present the ark going ahead into the Jordan (3:11), which is the start of the "how." Verse 3:11 is told after 3:12, and Joshua's thought is split by an unrelated question.

rule.text: Every passage has a flow: the events of a story, the lines of a song, the steps of a letter's argument, the movement of a prophet's message. Papa Dorin moves the baker along that flow.
